message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each except one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you must match the top discard either by **color**, **number**, or **action**. 3. If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise, you can be challenged.) | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, the round ends. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, Wild = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. If the winner reaches or exceeds the target (e.g., 500), the game ends. Otherwise, start a new round with a fresh shuffle. | | **Special Rules** | • **UNO Call** – When you have one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes a turn. Failure to do so results in a penalty of drawing two cards.
• **Challenge** – If you suspect a player illegally played a Wild Draw Four, you can challenge. If you’re right, the offender draws four cards; if wrong, you draw six. | | **Variations** | Many house rules exist (e.g., “Stacking” where Draw Twos/Wild Draw Fours can be stacked, “No Challenge” rules, etc.). Clarify before starting. | **Quick Tips** 1. Keep an eye on the colors you’re running out of; try to play them early. 2. Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. 3. Remember to shout “UNO!”—it’s a simple but crucial rule. That’s the core of Uno! Enjoy playing.
